meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well then, Victor, do you surrender?

examples.text: Русские не сдаются, особенно когда играют против олигархов.
examples.trans: Russians do not surrender, especially when playing against oligarchs.
Do not call me an oligarch.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Русские не сдаются, особенно когда играют против олигархов.
examples.trans: Russians do not surrender, especially when playing against oligarchs.

examples.text: Сколько тебе надо будет мяса продать, чтобы рассчитаться?
examples.trans: How much meat will you have to sell to settle up with me?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'wine' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Говядина в коробках, свинина в тушах, забирайте.
examples.trans: Beef in boxes, pork in carcasses, take them.

examples.text: Пожалуйста, извините за мой внешний вид.
examples.trans: You are welcome, excuse my appearance.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, бутылочка красного вина, лучшая в нашей винотеке.
examples.trans: Good evening, a bottle of red wine, the best in our cellar.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'быть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgot', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.trans: Ah, I forgot, sorry, just a cook.
Max, I forgot about the wine.
Don't forget to wash the toilet.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'sixty', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Sixty-five thousand rubles.
One hundred sixty over ninety.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'five', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты сказал, что уезжаешь, ты опять меня обманул.
examples.trans: You said you were leaving, you deceived me again.
Are you worked up again?
Sixty-five thousand rubles.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'thousand' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Sixty-five thousand rubles.
That means thousands of jobs.
A thousand roubles.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'rubles' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Sixty-five thousand rubles.
This costs a hundred roubles.
I haven't got a single rouble.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: One minute remains until the end of the match.
I'll be there in ten minutes.
Just a minute!

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'remains', paired with 'остаться'.

examples.trans: The advance stays with us.
I'm staying at home.
And the advance stays with us.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'until', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сколько тебе надо будет мяса продать, чтобы рассчитаться?
examples.trans: How much meat will you have to sell to settle up with me?

examples.text: Рядом с женщиной должен быть мужчина, на которого можно опереться.
examples.trans: Next to a woman there should be a man she can lean on.
Are you satisfied? You ruined the surprise.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'end' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я теперь буду тут работать до конца отпуска.
examples.trans: I am going to work here now until the end of my vacation.

examples.text: А ещё мне интересно, чем закончится этот сериал.
examples.trans: And I am also curious how this soap opera will end.
Of course there never will be.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'match' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You need to be more careful behind the wheel.
And not to engage in charity.

examples.text: Да и за подчинёнными нужно присматривать.
examples.trans: And I also have to keep an eye on the subordinates.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Сколько тебе надо будет мяса продать, чтобы рассчитаться?
examples.trans: How much meat will you have to sell to settle up with me?
No need, do not thank me.

examples.text: Любимая, жду тебя в машине, на работу надо возвращаться.
examples.trans: Darling, I am waiting for you in the car, you need to return to work.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Vitya, we need to talk.
Vitya, I want to talk.
Talk to him.

meanings.en: to step aside, to move back
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ойти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'step aside', paired with 'отходить'.

examples.text: Вика, отойди, мне ничего не видно.
examples.trans: Vika, step aside, I cannot see anything.
Step back from the car!
He stepped over to the window.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That is alright, you will get used to it.

examples.text: Во-первых, между нами ничего не было.
examples.trans: First of all, there was nothing between us.

examples.text: У нас с Катей ничего нет и не было.
examples.trans: There is nothing and never was anything between Katya and me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Русские не сдаются, особенно когда играют против олигархов.
examples.trans: Russians do not surrender, especially when playing against oligarchs.
Do not call me an oligarch.

examples.text: А как же мне тебя называть?
examples.trans: Then what should I call you?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы с тобой давно не виделись.
examples.trans: You and I have not seen each other in a long time.

examples.text: Я не хочу больше тебя видеть.
examples.trans: I do not want to see you anymore.

examples.text: Когда я тебя увидел, сразу всё понял.
examples.trans: When I saw you, I immediately understood everything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Русские не сдаются, особенно когда играют против олигархов.
examples.trans: Russians do not surrender, especially when playing against oligarchs.
The meat king of Russia?
Alright then, let us show our cards.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Chef, and did you win a lot?
We've done a lot.
Too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ты так и не научился играть в покер.
examples.trans: And you still have not learned to play poker.

examples.text: В таком случае мне здесь больше нечего делать.
examples.trans: In that case, there is nothing left for me to do here.

examples.text: А это что такое? Тоже сюрприз для Феди?
examples.trans: And what is this? Also a surprise for Fedya?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'never', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Но больше так никогда не делай.
examples.trans: But never do that again.

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.
No! Never!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'do', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.text: В таком случае мне здесь больше нечего делать.
examples.trans: In that case, there is nothing left for me to do here.

examples.text: Сделайте мне кто-нибудь бутерброд с тунцом.
examples.trans: Someone make me a tuna sandwich.
We will make it right now, Victoria Sergeyevna.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well then, Victor, do you surrender?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ты так и не научился играть в покер.
examples.trans: And you still have not learned to play poker.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'wanted', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: What did you want?

I want coffee.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No, Lyova, no.

examples.text: Марин, у меня нет никаких романов на работе.
examples.trans: Marina, I do not have any romances at work.
No, this is just my driver.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'demand', paired with 'потребовать'.

examples.trans: I demand silence!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'his', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Give him my phone number.
Why did she call late yesterday?

examples.text: У Феди скоро день рождения, она звонила посоветоваться.
examples.trans: Fedya's birthday is coming up soon, she called to ask for advice.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fire, to dismiss', paired with 'увольнять'.

examples.trans: Otherwise the owner of the hotel will fire you.

examples.text: Сенечка, зайчик, я уволилась, как ты сказал.
examples.trans: Senechka, little bunny, I quit just as you said.

examples.text: И потребую, чтобы он тебя уволил.
examples.trans: And demand that he fire you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well then, Victor, do you surrender?

examples.text: Русские не сдаются, особенно когда играют против олигархов.
examples.trans: Russians do not surrender, especially when playing against oligarchs.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something; somehow', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Шеф, нужно срочно что-то делать с этим мясом.
examples.trans: Chef, we urgently need to do something with this meat.
Is something wrong with the baby?
Has something happened?

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'child / baby' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I am ready to accept this child.

examples.text: Я точно знаю, что это мой ребёнок.
examples.trans: I know for sure that this is my child.
It is dangerous for the baby.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'адиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'sit down', paired with 'сесть'.

examples.trans: Sit down, please.
Sit down and hold the door.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'корее').

examples.text: У Феди скоро день рождения, она звонила посоветоваться.
examples.trans: Fedya's birthday is coming up soon, she called to ask for advice.
Call an ambulance!
Sit down quickly, Vika!
